findings.label: OIDC cleanup unreachable
findings.detail: delete_cluster reads cluster.identity.oidc.issuer from describe-cluster AFTER 'eksctl delete cluster --wait' has removed the cluster, so the branch never fires and prints 'no OIDC issuer recorded' instead. Re-running cannot repair it: the second pass returns early at 'cluster not found'. Both OIDC providers survive a teardown that reports no problem. Fix: hoist the issuer lookup above the eksctl delete and cache it.

findings.label: DRY_RUN masks the OIDC bug
findings.detail: Under DRY_RUN=1 the cluster still exists, so the OIDC branch resolves and prints 'deleting OIDC provider arn:...' — a dry run advertises behaviour the real run will not perform. Fixing finding 1 removes the divergence.

findings.label: Single-cluster teardown has region-wide scope
findings.detail: delete_load_balancers, delete_ebs_volumes and delete_security_groups enumerate the whole region and accept any resource tagged Project=XamOps regardless of which cluster was named, so './teardown.sh xamops-test-2' can delete xamops-test-1's security groups, detached volumes and load balancers. Bounded today (the live account inventory shows the only Project=XamOps resources are these two clusters' stacks, ASGs and roles). Fix: require the kubernetes.io/cluster/<cluster> tag in those three sweeps.

findings.label: Tag guard is a substring match
findings.detail: has_required_tag_list uses [[ "$tags" == *"Project=XamOps"* ]], which also matches Project=XamOpsProd or any longer value. Extract the tag value and compare it exactly.

findings.label: Log-group deletion is unguarded
findings.detail: delete_log_groups deletes by name prefix with no tag check, contradicting the 'every resource is checked for the tag Project=XamOps' claim in the script header and in README.md. Add the check or amend both claims.

findings.label: SC2318 wrong-target risk in delete_log_groups
findings.detail: 'local cluster="$1" lg="/aws/eks/${cluster}/cluster"' expands ${cluster} before the local assignment takes effect, so it resolves to the global loop variable — currently the same value, which masks the defect. Called with a $1 that differs from the enclosing loop variable, the first half of the function would delete one cluster's log group while the second half targets the other's. Split into two local statements.

findings.label: Teardown always exits 0
findings.detail: No 'set -e' and no exit-code accumulation; the 'Teardown pass finished' line prints regardless of failed steps or SKIPPED entries, so a caller cannot distinguish a clean pass from a partial one. Track a failure flag and exit non-zero.

findings.label: Teardown never executed
findings.detail: No DRY_RUN=1 pass appears anywhere in the evidence; the first execution would be the real one. The stated criterion covers the script's properties (executable, idempotent, refuses untagged), which are establishable by reading, so this is a finding rather than a rejection. Reviewer parsed it clean under bash 3.2.57 and 5.x in place of a run. Run DRY_RUN=1 ./teardown.sh before the real teardown.

findings.label: DRY_RUN=1 writes to kubeconfig
findings.detail: 'aws eks update-kubeconfig' in drain_k8s_cloud_resources is not wrapped in run(), so a preview still rewrites the local kubeconfig and switches the current context, against the header's 'change nothing'. Wrap it or guard the whole function.

findings.label: Stale note in verification.md
findings.detail: Section 2 says xamops-test-1.yaml 'still declares desiredSize: 2'; the file was subsequently updated to desiredCapacity: 4. The next reader would scale up a cluster already at 4. Update the note.

findings.label: Unbudgeted audit-log ingest
findings.detail: Both clusters enable api/audit/authenticator/controllerManager/scheduler logging at 7-day retention. CloudWatch ingest for audit is outside README.md's 'control planes plus four small nodes' cost claim. Note it, or drop audit while the clusters idle.

findings.label: Public API endpoint and public node IPs
findings.detail: clusterEndpoints.publicAccess: true with no publicAccessCIDRs, and privateNetworking: false puts nodes in public subnets with public IPs. IAM-authenticated and ssh.allow: false, so ordinary public-EKS exposure — but a new internet-reachable control-plane endpoint in a live account with no CIDR restriction. Restrict publicAccessCIDRs or keep the cluster lifetime short.

findings.label: Live shared credential restated
findings.detail: The doc quotes the shared agent API key verbatim and confirms by live curl that it returns the account's OpenObserve credentials (those values are redacted). The key was already committed in xamops-agent/manifests, so there is no new exposure, but reference it by name instead. Per-cluster token rotation belongs in its own task.
